data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding were GBP 100.728m. The syndicate experienced a net prior year run-off deficit of GBP 3.0m in 2015 (adverse development / strengthening), which was comprised of a GBP 4.7m favourable movement on direct business partially offset by a GBP 7.7m adverse movement on reinsurance accepted business. The movements were driven by a combination of large loss development and adverse reinsurance accepted outcomes, with legacy large claims (e.g. mining landslide, contractor and power claims) cited as contributors.
raw_causal_phrases: A surplus/(deficit) run-off deviation of (GBP 3.0) million was experienced in 2015 (2014: GBP 1.3 million surplus).

This was made up of a surplus on the prior year claims provisions of GBP 4.7 million on direct business (2014: GBP 2.0 million surplus) and a GBP 7.7 million deficit on reinsurance accepted business (2014: GBP 0.7 million deficit).

There have been a number of large claims which have contributed to this result. These include a loss of plant and equipment in a mining landslide, a contractor's liability claim and a number of power claims.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening reserves and the prior year run-off deviation were extracted from the Claims Outstanding note and the narrative 'surplus/(deficit) run-off deviation' text. The run-off split between direct and reinsurance accepted business is stated in the narrative and treated as gross amounts as presented. The claims development triangle provided in the report is a NET triangle (not gross) and therefore was not used to compute gross prior year development; it is included as a net triangle in _claims_triangle. Some specific large claims are described generically (e.g. 'mining landslide') rather than by formal event name and no per-event gross amounts were quantified in the text.
